newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks mixed ahead Fed's policy meeting.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks mixed ahead Fed's policy meeting.

text.p: Stock prices were mixed Monday as Wall Street turned cautious ahead of the two-day meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting group.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 22.32 points at 6,790.77. In the broader market, advances led declines by a small margin on volume of about 268 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 0.82 to 1,380.67, and the American Stock Exchange index was up 1.32 at 590.09.
Analysts said late-session volatility on Friday and general investor caution after the blue-chip index's surge of 360 points in January made investors wary of making big bets.
"The overall market is stuck in a little vacuum," said John Wosczyna, market strategist at Roney & Co.

Although the consensus is that the Federal Open Market Committee will hold interest rates steady at its meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday, Wall Street remained cautious and it was keeping some traders sidelined, analysts said.

The mixed tone in stocks came while the bond market posted solid gains following a lower-than-expected report on the National Association of Purchasing Management index. The January NAPM index was 52.0 against a revised reading of 53.8 in December.
Analysts said the data suggested the manufacturing sector will likely slow down in the first quarter.

In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 19/32 of a point, which lowered its yield to 6.74 percent from Friday's close of 6.79 percent. The yield and the price move in opposite directions.
Analysts said the NAPM data in itself was not enough to raise concern on Wall Street over future corporate profits.
But some analysts said worries that corporate profits could be squeezed in 1997 by slower economic growth and rising wage costs might be a factor weighing on stocks.
"I think there's still concern about the outlook for profit margins especially," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research.
Friday's late-session volatility, that saw the Dow index drop into negative ground, shoot up sharply and then end with an 11-point loss, could have spooked some traders, analysts said.
"I think the intra-day volatility scared a lot of people," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford, referring to Friday's trading. "It keeps everybody pretty edgy."
Also hanging over investors is this Friday's report on January employment levels.
Among individual stocks, Transocean Offshore Inc. fell 5-1/8 to 60-3/8 after saying its preliminary fourth-quarter results were below Wall Street expectations.
Scotsman Industries Inc. said it agreed to acquire Kysor Industrial Corp. in a cash tender offer of $43 for each Kysor share. Scotsman rose 1-7/8 to 25-7/8 and Kysor shot up 5-1/2 to 42-1/2.
Kysor also said it entered into a definitive agreement for the simultaneous sale of the assets of its Transportation Products Group to Kuhlman Corp. for $86 million. Kuhlman gained 7/8 to 18-5/8.
Apple Computer Inc. was flat at 16-5/8 after the Wall Street Journal reported the company was considering selling key business units to step up its cost-cutting efforts.
